 QWER Singapore 2027: 2 Shows, S$158-S$308 Tickets [2026]
 Tom Vance 
 Updated Oct 30, 2026 · 15 min read 
 QWER will play two Singapore shows on 8 and 9 January 2027 under the banner QWER 2nd TOUR ROCKATION : ROCKET LAUNCH!! , according to the Setlist.fm event page . Both nights sit at The Theatre at Mediacorp, and listed ticket prices run from S$158 to S$308.

 The sale calendar is already moving. BAWIGE 2nd Membership Pre-Sale registration opens today, 30 October 2026, at 12:00 p.m. and closes on 1 November at 12:00 p.m. The pre-sale itself runs on 10 November, and general sales start on 11 November at 10:00 a.m. through ticketmaster.sg.
 We file this story under hardware because the hard part of a modern concert sale is a device and network problem. A phone, a stable connection and a ready payment method decide who gets through a queue. Our hardware coverage tracks that side of the industry, and this piece applies it to a very specific 10-day sales window.

 One caution before the details. The dates, times, prices and sale windows below come from event listings and social-media posts. No official promoter or venue announcement turned up in the sources we could check, and no named speaker has given an on-record quote. Where a detail is missing, this article says so instead of filling the gap.

 The confirmed core is short and clear. Two shows, two consecutive nights, one venue. The tour title is QWER 2nd TOUR ROCKATION : ROCKET LAUNCH!!, and Singapore closes the run. The tour announcement placed Singapore as the final stop after Hong Kong on 2 January 2027.

 That closing position matters for fans. Final stops on a tour often carry extra weight, since the band has the whole run behind it and the crew has had months to tighten the production. We cannot say what QWER will play, because no setlist or production detail has been published. What we can say is that Singapore gets the last two nights of the tour, based on the announced route.
 The band itself is four members: Chodan, Magenta, Hina and Siyeon, as named in a July report by Starnews Korea . That report said QWER announced the second tour on social media on 12 July, and it described a poster showing a guitar-shaped rocket against a cosmic background, with the four members drawn in spacesuits. The tour name carries the same rocket theme.
 Here is the full fact base for Singapore, as listed.
 Tour: QWER 2nd TOUR ROCKATION : ROCKET LAUNCH!!
 Dates: 8 and 9 January 2027
 Venue: The Theatre at Mediacorp
 Times: 8:00 p.m. on 8 January, 6:00 p.m. on 9 January
 Ticket prices: S$158 to S$308
 General sales: 11 November 2026, 10:00 a.m., ticketmaster.sg
 Show Dates, Times and Venue at The Theatre at Mediacorp
 The first show falls on Friday, 8 January 2027, with an 8:00 p.m. listing. The second lands on Saturday, 9 January, at 6:00 p.m. The two start times differ by two hours, and that gap is the first practical detail for anyone planning travel.
 A Friday night start at 8:00 p.m. suits people who work a normal day and head to the venue afterward. The Saturday slot at 6:00 p.m. gives visitors from outside Singapore a cleaner evening, since they can see the show and still catch a late dinner or an early-morning flight the next day. Fans who attend both nights will see two different clock settings, so a single alarm or reminder will not cover both.
 The venue is The Theatre at Mediacorp. Event listings place it at 1 Stars Avenue, Singapore 138507. We found no verified capacity figure, no seating chart and no ticket-category breakdown in the available results, so any claim about how many fans fit inside would be a guess. The listings also leave open how the S$158 to S$308 range maps onto specific seating zones.
 Theatre-style venues usually seat fans in fixed rows rather than letting everyone crowd a standing floor. That is a general feature of the format and not a confirmed detail for these shows. Until a seat map appears, treat any talk of standing zones or reserved blocks as unverified.
 Ticket Prices: What S$158 to S$308 Means in Practice
 The listed range spans S$150 from bottom to top. The top price is about 1.95 times the cheapest, which suggests a meaningful spread between seating or package categories. No source names those categories, though, so the arithmetic below shows cost exposure and not value per seat.
 Scenario Lowest listed price Highest listed price 
 One ticket, one show S$158 S$308 
 Two tickets, one show S$316 S$616 
 One ticket, both shows S$316 S$616 
 Two tickets, both shows S$632 S$1,232 
 Four tickets, one show S$632 S$1,232 
 The figures are simple multiplication of the listed S$158 and S$308 endpoints. They exclude any booking fees, delivery charges or taxes that ticketmaster.sg may add at checkout, because none of those amounts appear in the sources. Budget a margin above the table values and check the final checkout total before paying.
 Fans who plan to attend both nights face a real decision. Doubling the spend buys two different evenings with two different start times, but the sources do not say whether the setlist changes between shows. Without that information, the case for a second night rests on the finale atmosphere and not on promised content.
 A KpopVisage event listing tracks the Singapore date, and fans can compare it against the ticketmaster.sg page once sales open. If the two ever disagree on a price or time, the ticketing page should win.
 BAWIGE Pre-Sale and Registration Timeline
 The sale runs in three steps. Registration for the BAWIGE 2nd Membership Pre-Sale opens first, then the pre-sale itself, then general sales. The listing ties early access to BAWIGE membership, so fans who want the pre-sale need to register inside the window or lose the early slot.
 Stage Opens Closes Length 
 Pre-sale registration 30 Oct 2026, 12:00 p.m. 1 Nov 2026, 12:00 p.m. 48 hours 
 BAWIGE 2nd Membership Pre-Sale 10 Nov 2026, 10:00 a.m. 10 Nov 2026, 11:59 p.m. about 14 hours 
 General sales (ticketmaster.sg) 11 Nov 2026, 10:00 a.m. Not listed Open-ended 
 Show 1 8 Jan 2027, 8:00 p.m. Not applicable Friday 
 Show 2 9 Jan 2027, 6:00 p.m. Not applicable Saturday 
 Two numbers stand out. Registration lasts exactly 48 hours, which punishes anyone who reads the news late. The pre-sale lasts less than 14 hours, from 10:00 a.m. to 11:59 p.m. on a single Tuesday, 10 November. Both windows are short enough that a missed calendar entry can cost a fan their first shot.
 Nine days separate the end of registration from the start of the pre-sale. That gap likely gives organizers time to verify registrations and issue access, though the sources do not describe their process. Fans should check their email and account pages during that stretch for any instructions, since a registration that never converts into pre-sale access is the kind of problem better caught early.
 The timing also means the full run from today to the first show is 70 days. From the general-sale date to the first show is 58 days. Anyone booking flights or hotels will want to wait for confirmed tickets, since the 11 November date arrives well before most budget fares drop for January travel.
 General Sale on ticketmaster.sg: 11 November at 10:00 a.m.
 General sales open on Wednesday, 11 November 2026, at 10:00 a.m. through ticketmaster.sg. The pre-sale window closes at 11:59 p.m. the night before, so there is only about ten hours between the two events. Whatever inventory the pre-sale leaves unsold flows into the general sale.
 We cannot say how many tickets will remain. No source gives total allocation, pre-sale allocation or per-account purchase limits. That absence is the biggest unknown for fans who skip the pre-sale and plan to buy on the morning of 11 November. If the pre-sale takes a large share, the general sale may be thin. If it takes a small share, the general sale could be the main event. Nobody outside the promoter can tell yet.
 The safest reading is to treat the general sale as a second chance and not a plan. Fans who care about specific seats should register for the pre-sale before the 1 November deadline, then use the general sale as a fallback.

 Where Singapore Sits on the ROCKET LAUNCH!! Route
 Starnews Korea reported that the second tour visits nine cities across Asia, starting in Seoul in September and ending in Singapore in January 2027. Its route list gives a useful frame for what Singapore represents.
 City Date(s) reported Shows 
 Seoul 12 and 13 Sept 2026 2 
 Taipei 10 and 11 Oct 2026 2 
 Fukuoka 13 Oct 2026 1 
 Osaka 15 Oct 2026 1 
 Tokyo 17 Oct 2026 1 
 Kuala Lumpur 7 Nov 2026 1 
 Bangkok 14 Nov 2026 1 
 Hong Kong 2 Jan 2027 1 
 Singapore 8 and 9 Jan 2027 2 
 By our count of those dates, the tour totals 12 shows. Three cities get two nights each: Seoul, Taipei and Singapore. The other six get one. Singapore therefore sits in the top tier of the schedule by show count, alongside the opening city and Taipei.
 A six-day gap before the finale
 Hong Kong plays on 2 January and Singapore opens on 8 January, a six-day gap. After Bangkok on 14 November, the tour also pauses for about seven weeks before Hong Kong. That break splits the tour into a busy autumn leg and a compact January close. Whether the band uses the pause to adjust the show is unknown, and we will not guess.
 Seoul to Singapore: nearly four months
 From the opening Seoul show on 12 September to the Singapore finale on 9 January is about four months. Fans in Singapore are the last in the region to see the full tour, which gives them the benefit of reviews and setlist reports from earlier stops. That is a real advantage for anyone deciding whether to buy a second night.
 Historical Context: From the 2025 World Tour to ROCKET LAUNCH!!
 Starnews Korea noted that the new tour follows the band’s debut world tour last year, titled 2025 QWER 1ST WORLD TOUR ROCKATION. That earlier run covered performances in North America and Asia. The second tour keeps the ROCKATION name and adds the ROCKET LAUNCH!! subtitle, which the outlet translated as a symbol of the band’s ambition to spread its music to a wider world.
 The second tour, by contrast, as reported, is an Asia-only itinerary. The route list names nine Asian cities and no North American dates. That narrower scope does not by itself say anything about demand, since the sources give no attendance or sales figures for either tour. It does show the band concentrating its second outing on its home region and nearby markets.
 Singapore’s return is also worth reading as a repeat. The headline framing of QWER returning to Singapore suggests the band has played the city before, but the sources we verified do not give dates, venues or crowd sizes for any earlier Singapore show. We therefore leave that history alone and stick to the January 2027 facts.
 What Remains Unconfirmed
 Several details a fan would want are missing from the available listings.
 Official promoter statement: none identified beyond the cited listings and social-media posts.
 Venue announcement: none identified from The Theatre at Mediacorp itself.
 Seat map and ticket categories: not published in the results we checked.
 Per-account ticket limits: unknown.
 Fees at checkout: unknown, so the totals in our price table exclude them.
 Setlist and production details: none announced.
 On-record quotes: no named speaker has been quoted in the sources.
 Early reporting on the sale was also incomplete at first. Ticket details were initially reported as pending before the schedule and prices were filled in. That pattern is common for fresh announcements and it explains why you may still see older pages with blank price fields. When two pages disagree, the more recently updated ticketmaster.sg page is the one to trust.
 Sale-Day Readiness: Devices and Network
 A short sale window rewards preparation more than speed. The pre-sale runs about 14 hours and registration lasts 48. Neither is a flash sale measured in seconds, yet both reward fans who arrive with a working account, a charged phone and a tested connection.
 Phone and browser
 Use the device you trust most. A mid-range handset handles a ticketing checkout fine, and our Galaxy A37 review looks at one such phone priced at $489.99. Fans upgrading before the show for better low-light photos can also look at the Motorola Signature 27 , which launches internationally on 5 November. Check the venue’s own rules on cameras before relying on any phone zoom. Those rules were not in the sources.
 Update your browser and app ahead of time, log in at least a day early, and save your payment details. A password reset or a failed card verification on sale morning costs minutes you will not get back.
 Connection and DNS
 Wired or strong Wi-Fi beats a weak mobile signal. If your home router has been flaky, switch to a stable connection before 10 November. Readers who want a cleaner resolver setup can follow our DNS over HTTPS guide , a 12-step, 60-minute job. It will not jump you ahead in a queue, but it removes one more variable from the morning.

 Buy only through ticketmaster.sg, the sales channel named in the listing. Resale pages and social-media offers can look convincing, and the sources give no sign of an authorized resale partner.
 Market Impact on Singapore’s K-Pop Live Calendar
 Two nights at one theatre is a measured footprint. It is smaller than the stadium-style bookings that headline the biggest regional tours, and the sources do not report capacity, so we avoid putting a revenue figure on the run. The one hard number we can compute is the ceiling for a single buyer: S$1,232 for two top-price tickets to both nights.
 The shows land in a busy season for live events in the region. Fans tracking Singapore’s Korean-culture events can use the KBeats Singapore events calendar to see what else is scheduled around January, and organizers elsewhere are chasing the same audience. Our own coverage of PLAYCON 2026 in Malta shows how smaller expos lean on free entry to win attendance, a very different model from a priced, pre-sale-driven concert.
 For Ticketmaster Singapore, the QWER dates are another high-attention on-sale during the 10 to 11 November stretch. Nobody has published traffic expectations, so we will not claim the platform will queue or crash. We simply note that a pre-sale followed by a general sale 10 hours later concentrates demand into two back-to-back mornings.
 Competitive Comparison: Singapore Against Other Tour Stops
 Compare Singapore with the other double-night stops. Seoul opens the tour with two shows on 12 and 13 September. Taipei hosts two on 10 and 11 October. Singapore matches them with 8 and 9 January. The remaining six cities each get one night, based on the Starnews Korea route.
 That puts Singapore at the same level as the opening city and Taipei, and above Kuala Lumpur, Bangkok and Hong Kong, which each get one show. For Southeast Asian fans, Singapore and its two nights is the only double-date stop in the region on the reported schedule. Fans in Kuala Lumpur and Bangkok play the same tour on single nights in November.
 Cross-border demand is the obvious consequence. A fan in Kuala Lumpur or Bangkok who misses their home date has Singapore as the next Southeast Asian option, and Hong Kong six days earlier as another. That is a reading of the schedule, not a measured trend, and we found no data on how many fans travel between these cities.
 Predictions for the Sale and the Finale
 These are our analysis, built from the schedule above, and none of them is a confirmed fact.
 The pre-sale will carry the heaviest demand. A 14-hour window that follows a 48-hour registration funnels the most motivated fans into one day. Expect the busiest moments right at 10:00 a.m. on 10 November.
 The cheapest and most central categories will move first. With a 1.95x spread between S$158 and S$308, price-sensitive fans will chase the low end and seat-focused fans will chase the best rows. Which category empties first depends on a seat map nobody has seen.
 More sale detail will appear before 10 November. Seat maps, category names and purchase limits usually surface before a pre-sale. If they do not, fans should treat that silence as a reason to register early and ask the ticketing page directly.
 Unofficial resale listings will show up fast. Any sale with a short window attracts them. Stick to ticketmaster.sg and ignore offers that arrive by direct message.
 A third Singapore date is unlikely without an announcement. The reported route ends in Singapore on 9 January. Unless a promoter says otherwise, plan around two nights.
 Pre-Sale Checklist Before 10 November
 Put these dates in your calendar today.
 Register for the BAWIGE 2nd Membership Pre-Sale before 12:00 p.m. on 1 November.
 Check your email and account between 2 and 9 November for access details.
 Log in and test your payment method the day before the pre-sale.
 Open the sale page at 10:00 a.m. on 10 November. The window closes at 11:59 p.m. the same day.
 Keep 11 November, 10:00 a.m. free as a general-sale backup.
 Decide your ceiling in advance using the table above, and add a margin for fees.
 The takeaway: QWER’s Singapore finale has a firm date, a firm venue and a firm sale calendar, but it is missing the seat map and allocation details that would let fans plan with confidence. Registration closes first, in about two days. Everything else follows from that one deadline.
 FAQ: QWER Singapore Concert 2027
 When is the QWER Singapore concert?
 QWER plays two shows on 8 and 9 January 2027. The first starts at 8:00 p.m. on Friday and the second at 6:00 p.m. on Saturday, as listed.
 Where will QWER perform in Singapore?
 Both shows are listed at The Theatre at Mediacorp, at 1 Stars Avenue, Singapore 138507, according to event listings.
 How much do QWER Singapore tickets cost?
 Listed prices range from S$158 to S$308. Booking fees and category details were not published in the sources, so the final cost may differ at checkout.
 When do QWER Singapore tickets go on sale?
 The BAWIGE 2nd Membership Pre-Sale runs on 10 November 2026 from 10:00 a.m. to 11:59 p.m. General sales begin on 11 November 2026 at 10:00 a.m. via ticketmaster.sg.
 How do I register for the BAWIGE pre-sale?
 Registration runs from 30 October 2026 at 12:00 p.m. to 1 November 2026 at 12:00 p.m. The sources do not detail the registration steps, so follow the instructions on the official listing or membership page.
 Is Singapore the last stop of the tour?
 Yes, based on the tour announcement. It identified Singapore as the concluding stop after Hong Kong on 2 January 2027.
 Is there a seating chart yet?
 No seating chart or ticket-category breakdown appeared in the available results. Check ticketmaster.sg closer to the sale.
 Has the promoter confirmed the shows?
 No official promoter or venue announcement was identified beyond the cited listings and social-media posts. The tour announcement itself came from QWER’s social channels, as reported by Starnews Korea.
